t.1.113.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by her, the king, knower of dharma, again spoke to the queen these excellent words, consonant with dharma.
t.1.113.2: Thus indeed did Vyuṣitāśva do this long ago, O Kuntī, just as you have said, O fair lady; for he was like an immortal.
t.1.113.3: But now I shall declare this dharma to you; learn from me this ancient dharma, as it was seen by the great-souled seers who knew dharma.
t.1.113.4: In former times, it is said, women were unconfined, O fair-faced one; they roamed and took their pleasure as they wished, and they were independent, O lovely-eyed one.
t.1.113.6: And that very ancient dharma is followed even today by creatures born in the wombs of animals, free from desire and hatred. This dharma, seen in ancient times, is honored by the great seers.
t.1.113.5: Though they strayed from their husbands from maidenhood onward, O fortunate one, there was no unrighteousness in them, O lady of lovely hips, for that indeed was righteousness in former times.
t.1.113.7: And among the Northern Kurus, O fair-thighed one, it is practiced even today; for that eternal dharma is one that shows favor to women.
t.1.113.9: There was a great seer named Uddālaka, so we have heard. He had a son, a sage, who was known as Śvetaketu.
t.1.113.10: This boundary was established among men by him out of anger, so we have heard; O lotus-petal-eyed one, learn from me the reason for it.
t.1.113.8: But in this world, O sweetly smiling one, this boundary of conduct was established not long ago; hear from me in detail by whom it was established and for what reason.
t.1.113.12: Then the seer's son, unable to bear it, became angry, seeing his mother thus being led away as if by force.
t.1.113.11: Long ago, it is said, a brāhmaṇa seized Śvetaketu's mother by the hand in full view of his father and said, "Let us go."
t.1.113.13: But his father, seeing him angry, said to Śvetaketu: "Do not give way to anger, my son; this is the eternal dharma."
t.1.113.15: Then Śvetaketu, the son of the ṛṣi, could not tolerate that custom, and he established this boundary for women and men on earth.
t.1.113.14: For on earth the women of all the varṇas are unconfined; just as cows are, dear one, so are creatures, each abiding in its own kind.
t.1.113.16: From that time on, O fortunate lady, this boundary has been established among human beings, but not among other creatures; so we have heard.
t.1.113.17: From this day forward, for a woman who strays from her husband there shall be a sin, an evil equal to that of killing an embryo, bringing misery.
t.1.113.18: And likewise for a man who strays from his wife, a woman chaste since her maidenhood and devoted to her husband, this very same sin shall exist on earth.
t.1.113.20: Thus, O timid one, in former times this righteous boundary was firmly established by force by him, Śvetaketu, the son of Uddālaka.
t.1.113.21: And, O thou of thighs like the plantain stem, Madayantī, appointed by Saudāsa for the begetting of offspring, went to the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha; so we have heard.
t.1.113.19: And the wife who, enjoined by her husband for the sake of offspring, will not do so, upon her too this very same sin shall surely fall.
t.1.113.22: And from him the beautiful lady, the wife of Kalmāṣapāda, obtained a son named Aśmaka, out of her wish to do what was pleasing to her husband.
t.1.113.24: Therefore, having indeed considered all these reasons, you ought to carry out this righteous word of mine, O blameless one.
t.1.113.23: You know too, O lotus-eyed one, that our own birth came from Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, O timid one, for the increase of the lineage of the Kurus.
t.1.113.25: O princess of steadfast vows, in every season of her fertility a wife must not neglect her husband: thus do the knowers of dharma understand dharma.
t.1.113.27: Whatever a husband says to his wife, O princess, whether it be lawful or even unlawful, that must be done just so; thus the knowers of dharma know.
t.1.113.26: At all the other remaining times, it is said, a woman is entitled to her freedom. Good people declare this to be the ancient dharma.
t.1.113.28: Especially one who longs for a son, yet is himself deprived of the power to beget, as I am, O lady of faultless limbs, yearning to behold a son.
t.1.113.29: So too, fair lady, this joined palm of mine, its fingers and palms reddened, resembling a lotus petal, is raised to my head to win your grace.
t.1.113.30: By my command, O lady with beautiful hair, you ought to beget sons endowed with virtues from a twice-born man who excels in austerity. Through you, O broad-hipped one, may I attain the destiny of those who have sons.
t.1.113.31: Thus addressed, the fair-hipped Kuntī, devoted to what was dear and beneficial to her husband, then replied to Pāṇḍu, the conqueror of enemy cities.
t.1.113.32: When I was a girl in my father's house, appointed to the honoring of guests, I waited there upon a fierce brahmin of rigorous vows.
t.1.113.33: The one whose resolve in dharma is deeply hidden, whom men know as Durvāsas, that ascetic of rigorously disciplined self I gratified with every effort.
t.1.113.34: That blessed one announced to me a boon joined with a power of incantation; he gave me a collection of mantras and spoke these words to me.
t.1.113.35: Whatever god you summon with this mantra, whether he is unwilling or willing, he shall come under your power.
t.1.113.37: Permitted by you, O king, I would summon a god by that mantra, O royal sage, so that we two may have offspring, O mighty one.
t.1.113.36: Thus was I told then, O Bhārata, in my father's house by that brahmin, a true word; the time for it has now come.
t.1.113.38: Which god shall I summon? Tell me, O best of those who know the truth. Know that I stand ready for this rite, awaiting your permission.
t.1.113.39: This very day, O fair-hipped one, make the effort according to the rite; summon Dharma, O lovely one, for among the gods he is the one who partakes of merit.
t.1.113.40: In no way could our dharma ever be joined with adharma, O fair-hipped lady, and this world will think, 'This is dharma.'
t.1.113.41: He will without doubt be the most righteous of the Kurus, and the mind of one given by Dharma will never delight in unrighteousness.
t.1.113.43: Thus addressed by her husband, the excellent lady said, "So be it," and having saluted him and received his leave, she walked around him reverently, keeping him to her right.
t.1.113.42: Therefore, O you of the bright smile, holding dharma foremost and keeping yourself restrained, propitiate Dharma with worshipful offerings and incantations.
